checks.title: Security baselines deployed: Windows, Defender for Endpoint, Edge
checks.remediation: Create and assign the three security baselines from Endpoint security, on the current baseline version, and re-run after each baseline refresh.
checks.narrative: The baselines carry several hundred hardening settings Microsoft maintains. Without them a tenant depends on whatever a custom profile happened to include. Version currency is not checked here yet.

checks.title: BitLocker policy: required, XTS-AES 256, silent, TPM, keys escrowed
checks.pass: facts.bitlockerPolicyAssigned && facts.bitlockerRequireEncryption && facts.bitlockerXtsAes256Os && facts.bitlockerSilent && facts.bitlockerTpmStartup && facts.bitlockerEscrowRequired
checks.remediation: In the assigned disk encryption policy require device encryption, set XTS-AES 256 for the OS drive, hide the warning for other encryption so enablement is silent, require TPM at startup, and require the recovery key to be backed up to Entra before BitLocker turns on.
checks.narrative: A lost laptop with no encryption is a breach; with encryption and no escrowed key it is a brick with no way back. Silent enablement is what makes the policy reach every device rather than the ones whose users clicked through.

checks.title: Windows Firewall on for domain, private and public profiles
checks.remediation: Assign a firewall policy that enables the firewall on all three profiles, with inbound connections blocked by default.
checks.narrative: The host firewall is what stands between a laptop on hotel Wi-Fi and lateral movement. A profile left unmanaged can be turned off by any local admin or a legacy GPO.

checks.title: Windows LAPS: backup to Entra, password reset after use
checks.remediation: Assign an account protection LAPS policy with the backup directory set to Entra ID and a post-authentication action that resets the password.
checks.narrative: A shared local administrator password is the oldest lateral movement path there is. LAPS gives every device its own, stored where it can be audited and rotated after each use.

checks.title: Defender Antivirus: real-time, cloud, PUA, sample submission, scheduled scan
checks.remediation: Assign an antivirus policy from the Microsoft Defender Antivirus template with real-time and cloud-delivered protection on, PUA set to block, automatic sample submission, and a weekly scheduled scan.
checks.narrative: Defender's defaults are good; a policy makes them stick and makes them auditable. Cloud protection is where the detection logic actually lives, so a device with it off is running last year's engine.

checks.title: Tamper protection on
checks.remediation: In the Windows Security Experience policy set tamper protection to enabled (the value is 0 in the settings catalog) and assign it to all Windows devices.
checks.narrative: Malware that lands with admin rights first turns off the antivirus. Tamper protection takes that option away from everything except Intune and the Defender portal.

checks.title: Network protection in block mode
checks.remediation: Set network protection to block in the antivirus or attack surface reduction policy.
checks.narrative: Network protection blocks outbound connections to known malicious hosts from any process, not only the browser. In audit mode it reports and lets the traffic through.

checks.title: Attack surface reduction rules: every rule blocking, none off
checks.remediation: Assign an attack surface reduction policy that sets every rule to block (warn is accepted where Microsoft offers it). Rules still in audit need a dated plan recorded as an exception; raise the threshold in the profile while it runs.
checks.narrative: ASR rules stop the techniques phishing payloads use: Office spawning processes, scripts launching downloaded executables, credential theft from LSASS. Audit mode generates events and stops nothing. The effective state per device is a later collector; this is the policy.

checks.title: No ASR-only exclusions, or each documented
checks.remediation: Remove exclusions that are no longer needed and record the rest as object-level exceptions with an owner and a reason.
checks.narrative: An exclusion turns the rules off for a path. Attackers know the common ones.

checks.title: SmartScreen on in the shell, override blocked
checks.remediation: Set SmartScreen for the shell (Explorer) to enabled and prevent users from overriding file warnings, in a settings catalog or endpoint protection policy.
checks.narrative: SmartScreen checks downloaded files and installers against reputation before they run. The override setting is what stops a user from clicking Run anyway.

checks.title: Office macros from the internet blocked
checks.remediation: Deploy the Office ADMX-backed setting Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet for Word, Excel and PowerPoint at least, through a settings catalog policy or the Office cloud policy service.
checks.narrative: Microsoft blocks internet macros by default since 2022, but a user or an old GPO can turn that back on. A policy makes it enforced.

checks.title: Windows Hello for Business enabled
checks.remediation: Enable Windows Hello for Business in the tenant-wide enrollment settings or an identity protection policy, with a PIN minimum length and biometrics allowed.
checks.narrative: Hello for Business replaces the password at the device with a key bound to the TPM. It is the phishing-resistant method most users can have today.

checks.title: Cloud Kerberos trust configured for hybrid sign-in
checks.remediation: Set Use cloud trust for on-premises authentication in the Windows Hello for Business policy and create the Kerberos server object in Active Directory.
checks.narrative: Without cloud Kerberos trust, hybrid-joined devices need certificates or key trust to reach on-premises resources after a Hello sign-in, which is where most hybrid Hello deployments stall.

checks.title: Update rings with a quality update deadline, feature update profile assigned
checks.remediation: Assign an update ring with a quality update deadline within the threshold and a grace period, and a feature update profile that pins the Windows version in service. Update compliance per device is a later collector.
checks.narrative: A ring without a deadline is a suggestion. The deadline is what gets the patch installed on the laptop that never reboots.

checks.title: macOS FileVault policy with recovery key escrow
checks.remediation: Assign a macOS disk encryption or settings catalog policy that enables FileVault and escrows the personal recovery key to Intune.
checks.narrative: Same reasoning as BitLocker: the policy makes encryption universal and the escrow makes recovery possible. Rotation after a reveal is an effective-state check for later.

checks.title: macOS hardening: Gatekeeper, firewall, SIP required
checks.remediation: Enforce Gatekeeper and the application firewall through the settings catalog, and require System Integrity Protection in the macOS compliance policy.
checks.narrative: Gatekeeper and SIP are on by default and can be turned off by any admin user, which on most Macs is the user. The compliance policy is what notices.

checks.title: Platform SSO deployed on macOS
checks.remediation: Deploy the Platform SSO extension through a settings catalog policy with the Enterprise SSO plug-in, in Secure Enclave key or password sync mode.
checks.narrative: Platform SSO gives the Mac a device-bound credential the way Hello does on Windows, and makes the local account follow the Entra password. The mode in use is not recorded yet.

checks.title: Mobile: app protection assigned, jailbroken and rooted devices blocked
checks.remediation: Assign an app protection policy for each mobile platform in scope and a compliance policy that blocks jailbroken or rooted devices.
checks.narrative: App protection is what keeps company data inside managed apps on a phone the company does not own. Jailbreak detection is the compliance signal Conditional Access needs for the corporate ones.
